Happy to build that schedule. I don't see the event agenda yet, though. Could you paste it in or share a link? The session list with titles, times, and formats is all I need.

Once I have it, I'll:

1. **Filter** out anything starting before 10:00 and any roundtables.
2. **Pick AI-focused sessions**, including ones whose titles don't say "AI" but cover ML, LLMs, generative tools, data science, and similar topics.
3. **Resolve conflicts** where two good talks overlap. I'll pick one and list the other as a backup.
4. **Build in breaks** for lunch and travel time between rooms if the venue is large.

It would also help to know:
- **Your angle on AI**: technical deep dives, business strategy, ethics and policy, or a mix?
- **Your end time**: are you staying through the last session or leaving early?
- **Must-sees**: any specific speakers or sessions you already know you want?

Send the agenda and I'll put together a clean hour-by-hour plan.

{"id":"i-shipped-a-local-ai-model-to-7-000-user","title":"I shipped a local AI Model to 7,000+ users. Here's what happened.","start":"13:20","end":"14:00","room":"Ballroom 1","type":"talk","speakers":["Aditya Thakur"],"description":"Everyone loves the idea of running AI locally on a phone. Until they actually try shipping it. When I decided to add an AI-powered mock interview coach to SSB Prep, a Flutter app used by more than 7,000 students preparing for India's Services Selection Board (SSB) interviews, I assumed model integration would be the hardest part. It wasn't. The real challenges appeared after the model worked. How do users download a 1.4 GB model? Which devices can realistically run it? How do you prevent crashes on low-memory phones? What happens when your AI feature is larger than your app itself? And how do you build a voice-first experience around a local model that feels natural to users? In this talk,…"}

{"id":"beyond-prompts-context-memory-agent-loop","title":"Beyond Prompts: Context, Memory & Agent Loops for Reliable AI-Powered Flutter Apps","start":"14:15","end":"14:55","room":"Junior Ballroom","type":"talk","speakers":["Neelansh Sethi","Adil Shaikh"],"description":"Adding an LLM to a Flutter app is easy. Making that AI feature reliable enough to behave like part of a real product is much harder. A good prompt alone is rarely enough. The model needs the right application state, conversation history, user preferences, retrieved information and memory at the right moment. Once the model can use tools and take actions, we also need to control how it reasons, acts, observes results, recovers from failures and understands when to continue or stop. In this session, we'll build an AI-powered Flutter application and progressively evolve it from a simple LLM wrapper into a context-aware, tool-using agent.
